Your phone dies in the cold. So the cold broke your battery? Nope.
Guess: is the power gone, or hiding? Comment before the end.
Inside, tiny lithium ions swim from side to side. That's your power.

text: In the cold, the liquid they swim in gets thick. Like honey.

The ions slow down, so the battery drains faster.
Phones are made for zero to thirty-five degrees. Colder, and they can switch off.

text: At minus twenty, some batteries give only about half their power.
Twist: the power isn't gone. Warm it up, and battery life comes back.

Just don't charge it while it's freezing. That can damage it.

text: Hiding, not gone. Did you guess right? Yes or no?
